prompt:
Where is the localized surface plasmon (extinction maximum) of a 60 nm diameter Au sphere embedded in immersion oil, n = 1.515? Search between 500 and 700 nm.

---
Report your result by calling submit_answer with these values:
- `peak_wavelength_nm` (nm): vacuum wavelength of maximum extinction

concerns: I used Johnson–Christy optical constants for gold. The peak position depends on which gold dataset is used: McPeak (2015) data put it at about 549.5 nm, with an extinction cross-section of about 22,600 nm². Expect an uncertainty of about ±10 nm from this alone.

The Johnson–Christy data points are about 15 nm apart near 550 nm, and the solver interpolates linearly between them. The exact peak position is therefore only good to a few nm, even though the spectrum was sampled every 0.5 nm.

I assumed an ideal, isolated, perfectly spherical particle with bulk gold optical constants, lit by a plane wave, in uniform oil with n = 1.515 at every wavelength (no dispersion in the oil). I did not include extra electron damping from the particle surface, faceting, size spread or a ligand shell. Real colloids may show a peak a few nm away from this.
answer.summary: The extinction maximum (localized surface plasmon) of a 60 nm gold sphere in immersion oil (n = 1.515) is at about 559 nm vacuum wavelength. I got this from an exact Mie scattering calculation of a single sphere, scanning 500–700 nm in 0.5 nm steps with Johnson–Christy optical constants for gold. At the peak, the extinction cross-section is about 20,200 nm² (extinction efficiency 7.15). About two-thirds of that is absorption (13,500 nm²) and one-third scattering (6,700 nm²). With McPeak gold data instead, the peak comes out at about 549.5 nm, so the answer is roughly 550–560 nm depending on the gold data.

result.conventions:
Lightsmith conventions (fixed; changing them needs a schema version bump):
- Lengths in nm. Wavelengths are vacuum wavelengths in nm.
- Time dependence exp(-i omega t): absorbing materials have Im(eps) > 0 and Im(n) > 0.
- Cross sections in nm^2; efficiencies Q = C / (pi r_eq^2), r_eq = volume-equivalent radius of all particles.
- layer_stack / periodic: layers listed from the superstrate (incidence side) to the substrate; light travels +z.
  R is measured in the superstrate, T in the substrate.
- mode: cross-section in the xy plane, propagation along +z.
- device: ports are planes whose normal is the axis where size_nm is zero; direction is into the device.
- problem.options[<method or backend name>] holds solver options, validated by that backend.
- Materials: {"kind": "constant_index", "n_real": .., "n_imag": ..}, {"kind": "library", "name": "Au"},
  drude, drude_lorentz, tabulated, constant_permittivity. FDTD needs dispersive models (fit_drude_lorentz).
- Results carry provenance and warnings: read the warnings before trusting the numbers.
